original_test_intent: Validate that an approved PCIe Data Link Protocol Error is detected as uncorrectable fatal at the intended link component and that platform containment, persistent reporting and recovery follow the engineering-approved policy.
original_method: Keep execution blocked. Future method maps link endpoints and detector, baselines AER severity/masks and recovery paths, generates one specified link-protocol violation, captures the last in-band and independent trace, verifies fatal status plus approved link/device/host containment, then recovers through OOB and proves boot, topology and device integrity.
manual_activity: The PCIe/platform owner defines the exact fatal protocol violation and detecting port, approves containment/reset and OOB recovery, supervises the single destructive stimulus and restores the platform.
required_inputs: Pinned NVIDIA PCIe RAS injector/spec/version/checksum and supported firmware/OS/topology
Endpoint/root-port/slot/BDF/link direction, detecting component and exact protocol violation
Injection command and proof it selects Data Link Protocol Error rather than Bad DLLP, Surprise Down or another bit
AER uncorrectable status/severity/mask/root reporting plus expected link/device/host fatal action and deadlines
Persistent BERT/CPER/firmware/SEL/reset-cause and independent trace requirements
OOB/console/boot recovery, device/data-integrity gates, aborts, clear policy and full restoration
safety_requirements: No stimulus until the fatal action and recovery contract are formally approved
Dedicated disposable SUT/workload with serial/OOB capture, recoverable boot media and platform/device owner present
Snapshot topology, AER masks/severity/status, link/device state, traffic/data and boot configuration
Inject one violation once; never retry automatically after fatal containment or evidence loss
Use only independent recovery; preserve persistent records before clears and abort on boot loop or unintended component impact
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only topology, AER severity/masks/status, link/device baseline, persistent logs and recovery readiness
Validate future protocol violation, detector and containment evidence mapping
Do not configure severity/masks, generate malformed protocol traffic, inject, clear, retrain/reset/power-cycle, recover, retry or judge result
engineer_actions: Author the exact Data Link Protocol Error procedure and fatal Criteria
Approve detector/link target, containment/reset, persistent evidence and recovery
Supervise one destructive event with OOB capture
Recover, validate topology/data/device and issue verdict

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Generate one defined protocol violation on one mapped link, capture detector-specific fatal AER and persistent evidence, then follow a preapproved OOB containment/recovery sequence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds violation identity, detecting component, fatal policy, persistent capture, recovery and data/device restoration to a label-only source.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Surprise Down, Bad DLLP or a software-set AER bit cannot substitute for a Data Link Protocol Error path.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The in-band OS and device may disappear immediately, so lack of persistent/OOB evidence can make a destructive run uninterpretable.

project_override_considerations: Firmware-first ownership and fatal-severity programming may determine whether the host resets or only the hierarchy is contained. The project must choose the expected action before execution, not after observing it.
expected_evidence: Baseline AER uncorrectable masks/severity/status, root reporting, topology, link/device and OOB capture
Exact one-shot fatal stimulus with last in-band and independent timestamped trace
Fresh Data Link Protocol Error at the intended detector plus approved fatal containment/reset and persistent BERT/CPER/SEL/reset-cause
Recovery deadlines, restored topology/link/device/driver/workload and verified data integrity with no unrelated impact

review_improvement: Adds exact protocol/detector identity and a persistent-evidence/OOB recovery model appropriate to a fatal link-layer event.
independent_technical_reasoning: A Data Link Protocol Error indicates a violation of link-layer protocol rules, not merely a corrupted packet or removed link. Fatal behavior depends on which port detects it and how severity/firmware-first policy is configured. Because the event can eliminate in-band access, the pass contract must be fixed beforehand and survive containment through persistent and independent capture.
